posts.text: Back in Washington and ready to deliver for the American people! https://t.co/iB2wgpJ8DP

Never Forget the Vet!

On Veterans Day, we honor and thank the brave men and women who have worn our nation’s uniform and sacrificed so much in service to our country.

But honoring our veterans must go beyond parades, flags, and words of gratitude. We have a solemn responsibility to ensure they receive the healthcare, mental health services, benefits, and support they have earned.

Our commitment to our veterans cannot be limited to one day a year. We must honor their service through action and ensure that no veteran is ever forgotten or left behind.

Thank you to all who have served. Happy Veterans Day!

Mobile Office Hours!

My staff is here to help with everything from obtaining a passport to Social Security and VA benefits and Service Academy nominations.

Come meet with my staff tomorrow, Thursday, November 12th, from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm at the Huntington Station Branch Library, 1335 New York Avenue, Huntington Station.
It’s not enough to just win elections. Now we have to actually deliver for the people that we represent. Read my Wall Street Journal op-ed here: https://t.co/RnPtXaEKu2 https://t.co/ZxwOUdbeK9

Today, we mark the 88th anniversary of Kristallnacht, the “Night of Broken Glass,” when Nazi mobs unleashed a wave of violence against Jewish communities across Germany and Austria, destroying synagogues, businesses, and homes.

Kristallnacht was a horrifying turning point in the persecution of European Jews and a stark reminder of the devastating consequences of unchecked antisemitism and hatred.

As we remember the victims, we must do more than remember. We must speak out against antisemitism wherever it occurs, confront hatred and intolerance in all their forms, and stand shoulder to shoulder with our Jewish friends and neighbors. Silence in the face of hatred is not an option. We all have a responsibility to ensure that the lessons of history are never forgotten.

Never forget. Never again.

ROAD TO 250: Long Island & Queens Legacies

Today marks the 315th birthday of Jupiter Hammon, born into slavery in 1711 at Lloyd Manor in present-day Lloyd Harbor. He went on to become America's first published Black poet, leaving a remarkable legacy that deserves to be remembered.

Back in 2020, I had the opportunity to visit historic Joseph Lloyd Manor, where Hammon lived and wrote for much of his life.

As part of our Road to 250, there's no better time to celebrate his life and contributions to American history.

Protecting Long Island's water has always been one of my top priorities.

I've worked to bring federal funding back to our district to clean up our bays, improve wastewater infrastructure, and remove harmful forever chemicals from our drinking water.

Between 2024 and 2026, nearly 6 million oysters were planted in Manhasset Bay, Hempstead Harbor, and Oyster Bay/Cold Spring Harbor using federal funding I secured. That includes 2 million oysters in Manhasset Bay alone!

I've also secured $1.092 million for wastewater improvements that will help protect Manhasset Bay, and millions more to help local water districts address PFAS contamination.

Anna Smith Strong, of Setauket, is believed to have helped the Culper Spy Ring by hanging laundry on her clothesline to send coded signals about secret meeting locations.

Her story reminds us that the fight for American independence wasn't just waged on battlefields. It happened right here in our own backyard!

As a first-generation Italian American and a member of the Congressional Italian American Caucus, I am proud of my heritage and the contributions Italian Americans have made to our great nation.

My father, Joseph A. Suozzi, lived an extraordinary American Dream. Born in Ruvo del Monte, Italy, he immigrated to the United States as a child, served as a navigator in the U.S. Air Force during World War II, and went on to serve as Mayor of Glen Cove and a Justice of the New York State Supreme Court’s Appellate Division.

To honor stories like his and preserve the contributions of generations of Italian Americans, I’ve introduced legislation to establish a National Museum of Italian American History and Culture.

My father’s story is one of countless immigrant success stories that helped build America. Let’s honor that legacy by fighting discrimination, expanding opportunity, and keeping the American Dream alive for future generations.

Never Forget the Vet!

On Veterans Day, we honor and thank the brave men and women who have worn our nation’s uniform and sacrificed so much in service to our country.

But honoring our veterans must go beyond parades, flags, and words of gratitude. We have a solemn responsibility to ensure they receive the healthcare, mental health services, benefits, and support they have earned.

Our commitment to our veterans cannot be limited to one day a year. We must honor their service through action and ensure that no veteran is ever forgotten or left behind.

Thank you to all who have served. Happy Veterans Day!
